purpose: Read container instance metadata via the agent introspection API. Returns Cluster name, ContainerInstanceArn, agent Version. Health-check + identity probe; first command to run when SSH'd into a container instance.
List all tasks running on this container instance. Shows Arn, DesiredStatus, KnownStatus, Family, Version, Containers[]. Diagnose 'why isn't my task running' from the agent's view.

Restart the ECS agent via ecs-init systemd unit. Required after editing /etc/ecs/ecs.config to pick up env-var changes. The agent container is destroyed + recreated; running tasks survive (managed by Docker daemon).

examples.invocation: sudo vi /etc/ecs/ecs.config; sudo systemctl restart ecs; sudo systemctl status ecs

purpose: Stream live agent logs. Format depends on ECS_LOG_OUTPUT_FORMAT (logfmt or json) and ECS_LOG_ROLLOVER_TYPE (size or hourly). Look for ACS connection state + task-state-change events.
Inspect the running ECS agent container. Shows env vars, mounts, network, restart policy. Most useful field: .Config.Env — confirms which ECS_* vars made it through ecs-init.
Force ecs-init to reload its cached agent container image. Used during agent-update rollback or when /var/cache/ecs/ecs-agent.tar is stale.

examples.invocation: sudo systemctl stop ecs; sudo /usr/libexec/amazon-ecs-init reload-cache; sudo systemctl start ecs

purpose: From INSIDE a task container, fetch the task's IAM-role credentials. The agent serves this endpoint; AWS SDKs auto-discover via the AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_RELATIVE_URI env var injected into the container.

examples.scenario: Debug 'AWS credentials not found' in a task

purpose: Transition a container instance to DRAINING — stops accepting new task placements; service-managed tasks are gradually replaced on other capacity. Standard pre-AMI-update / pre-scale-in workflow.
